My fear is that with the community getting bigger:

  • It will get easier and quicker to reach the 100CCP threshold as there are more users with upvoats to give. A slowish grind to the threshold is good for the community because it encourages participation etc etc. Should this threshold not be adjusted relative to the size of the community?

  • Because the threshold can be reached quicker more people will have plentiful upvoats and downvoats to give. I.e the currency of voats is devalued. We have inflation.

I'm not an economics expert but it seems to me that this is what will happen / is happening. Im sure there are smart people out there who can figure out the best way to manage this.

So my suggestions are:

  • Make the 100CCP threshold a calculated value which varies depending on the size of the community.

  • Give people who reach the threshold more upvoats and downvoats but they should still hit up against limits to retain the value of voats.

December 19th - The personal journal of Professor Jeremiah Day

Holden Caulfield. Over the past twenty years, through my time as a student, then on to being an aid, and during my internship and now during my march to tenure, you have been my unwilling but constant companion. I’ve watched generations of literary trends rise and fall the old being swept away by the new while the new fades into the old just to be swept away in a continuously endly cycle. But not you Holden. In every class, During every semester your ghost always finds its way into my stacks of unread student manuscripts. It’s never directly. No one ever sits down and tries to rewrite the Catcher in the Rye. That would be to obvious. But damn if they don’t side on either side of doing just that. On one side, you have the overwhelming angst of students trying so desperately to capture Salinger's style that they might as well be forcing his hand to their own situation. And on the other side, you have students trying so hard not to write like Salinger that they strip out any soul they have to avoid a trace of his voice.

And it’s not just him. Palahniuk, Bukowski, Thompson. If they write about drugs or use the f word more then once per page, then I’ll hear their shadows screaming at me from the pages. This has been the case since i started teaching and it will continue to be the case undoubtedly until I retire or just stop caring and award As to everyone just for showing up.

There were no As today, save for one. A student in my class, Paige Richardson actually managed to write something that didn’t make me was to tear the pages apart. For that she got an A and my eternal gratitude.

The tech out here where I work isn't anything very special, mostly piping, pressure gauges and liquid sensors. What I do think is really neat though, is the way everything out here works together. On a typical well, you have a generator, which powers a pumping unit (horse head). That pumping unit pulls oil, water, natural gas, and whatever else up out of the well, and sends it through the line to the separating equipment. The equipment separates the oil, gas, and water/junk. The oil goes into a rank for storing, as does the water. The natural gas that comes up is used to power ALL of the equipment (it's all pressure operated, not engine operated). Some of that natural gas is also used to power the generator, which is powering the pumping unit, and so on. I
